predecessors.note: PNG withdrew in early 1990 'leaving Bougainville in the control of the BRA'.

land.text: Bougainville, as an autonomous region under the 2001 peace agreement

successors.note: The first Autonomous Bougainville Government was elected in May and June 2005.

correction.text: Bougainville apart from Buka: 'By the end of 1990, the PNGDF national forces controlled Buka, while the BRA controlled the remainder of Bougainville'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the land the BRA held at the end of 1990 ('the BRA controlled the remainder of Bougainville' apart from Buka). It shrinks by the 1993 loss of Arawa and by the retaking of the north and southwest (1991-92, page imprecise); those moves are in the ledger and in the PNG dossier's contest zone. No area is given on the page.

ledger.note: 1990: Francis Ona declares Bougainville independent. 'Francis Ona, the leader of the BRA, unilaterally declared independence in May 1990'; 'Ona subsequently set up the Bougainville Interim Government (BIG), appointing himself president' (the page gives no date for that). PNG had withdrawn in early 1990.

region.text: the north and southwest of the main island

ledger.note: 1991: PNG forces start retaking the island. 'By 1991-92 [PNG] had retaken the north and southwest of the main island.'
1993: Arawa falls to PNG. 'PNG retook Arawa in February 1993'; by 1996 PNG held roughly 40% of the island with resistance forces.
1997: a truce. 'Talks in mid-1997 produced a truce'; the Lincoln Agreement was signed in January 1998.

2001: the peace agreement ends the secession. 'A peace agreement was reached in 2001'; the first Autonomous Bougainville Government was elected in May and June 2005. The page gives no date on which the BIG ceased.

wars.name: Bougainville Civil War
wars.outcome: Truce in mid-1997, Lincoln Agreement January 1998, peace agreement 2001; the BIG did not win independence; a non-binding referendum in late 2019 voted overwhelmingly for it (see the Papua New Guinea dossier).

certainty.note: De facto control: the page gives no front line, only 'the north and southwest' retaken by 1991-92 and Arawa in February 1993.

sources.title: Bougainville Civil War
sources.note: Everything here: BRA control, May 1990 declaration, BIG, PNG's retaking of land, 1997 truce, 2001 agreement.

notes: Written 2026-10-18 from the Bougainville Civil War page only. The page uses neither 'Republic of Bougainville' (kept in alt_names as the name of the 1990 declaration, unverified) nor gives a capital, a day for the declaration, or the BIG's end; the end year 2001 is the peace agreement's, with the first Autonomous Bougainville Government elected in 2005. Wikipedia title: none known for the BIG as a state (the BRA has its own article); left null. Capitals empty: page silent. A gap-filler should open 'Bougainville Revolutionary Army' or 'Autonomous Region of Bougainville' and the 1975 'Republic of the North Solomons' episode.
